q: Wavefront is always ________ to the direction of propagation (or) rays. 2025
e: A wavefront is defined as a surface passing through points of the same phase, which is always perpendicular to the direction of ray propagation.

q: Monochromatic light has a single ________. 2025
e: Monochromatic light is light that consists of a single wavelength.

q: Constructive interference has ________ intensity. 2025
e: Constructive interference occurs when light waves reinforce each other in phase to produce maximum intensity.

q: What type of wave emerges from a slit when a plane wave passes through a slit? 2026
e: According to Huygens' principle, a narrow slit acts as a new source producing circular or spherical wavelets.

q: If the path difference is ________ the waves will interfere destructively. 2025
e: Destructive interference occurs when the path difference between two waves is an odd multiple of half-wavelengths.

q: The angular position of a point of a periodic wave is called the ________. 2025
e: The phase angle describes the fractional part of a period or angular state of a wave at a given point.

q: Two positions are in phase if phase difference are ________. 2025
e: Two points are in phase when their phase difference is an even integer multiple of π.

q: Huygens' principle states that every point on a ________ may be considered as a source of secondary wavelets. 2025
e: Huygens' principle states that every point on a primary wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets.

q: What is the phase difference between two waves that are perfectly in phase? 2025
e: Waves that are perfectly in phase reach their peaks and troughs simultaneously, giving a phase difference of 0°.

q: If the violet light in Young's double slit experiment is replaced by red light, the fringe width will ________. 2025
e: Red light has a longer wavelength than violet light, and fringe width is directly proportional to wavelength.

q: When two waves are completely out of phase, what is their phase difference? 2025
e: Two waves are completely out of phase when their phase difference is 180° or π radians.

q: Constructive interference has ________ intensity. 2025
e: At points of constructive interference, wave amplitudes combine to produce maximum light intensity.

q: Which colour of light will have the smallest diffraction angle in a grating? 2025
e: Diffraction angle is proportional to wavelength, and violet light has the shortest wavelength in visible light.

q: If the path difference is ________ the waves will interfere destructively. 2025
e: A path difference equal to λ/2 results in complete destructive interference.

q: The position of fringes and fringe width depend on the ________ of light source. 2025
e: Fringe width in interference patterns depends directly on the wavelength of the light used.

q: In a double slit experiment, if the distance between the slits and the screen is increased, the fringe width will ________. 2025
e: Fringe width is directly proportional to the distance between the slits and the screen.

q: Monochromatic light means that it has a ________ wavelength. 2025
e: Monochromatic light consists of light rays of a single unique wavelength.

q: The bright and dark fringes in a diffraction pattern are created by ________ of diffracted light waves. 2026
e: Diffraction patterns are formed by the mutual interference of secondary wavelets originating from different parts of the same wavefront.

q: Slits per unit length in a diffraction grating is called ________. 2026
e: The number of lines or slits ruled per unit length on a grating is known as the grating constant.

q: What is the nature of the wavefront far away from the source? 2026
e: At very large distances from a source, a small section of a spherical wavefront appears as a plane wavefront.
